## Release — backlog-campaign v0.24.0

### ✨ What's new in v0.24.0

#### Leave-open campaigns that stay mergeable

- Issues whose narrowed touch paths overlap an open PR are now stacked on the tip of that PR's chain instead of branching from `main`, so merging one PR no longer turns its siblings into conflicts. Broad default paths (`src/**`, `scripts/**`) no longer trigger stacking on their own.
- The dashboard and a PR comment on each stacked child show the merge order ("merge #A, then #B (stacked on #A)…").
- After a parent is squash-merged, the child is retargeted to `main` and updated by merging `main` into it — never a rebase or force-push. Generated trees are rebuilt, source files get a real 3-way resolution, and the version stays above `main`'s.

#### Review that converges

- One review-convergence rule: at most three review rounds, then a `rethink` verdict instead of another automatic pass; later rounds look only at the fix commits; repeats of an already-posted finding become rechecks; findings on unchanged lines are tagged pre-existing and never block.
- Every BLOCK finding is independently verified. A BLOCK is downgraded only when the verifier refutes it; with no verification it stays blocking.
- New finding outcomes `wrong`, `intentional` and `not-worth` (each with a one-line reason), plus `rounds_to_lgtm` on merge and a per-V-code noise report (`bun run scripts/review-noise-report.ts --since 7d`) that flags rules to tune or to promote to a lint.
- User-visible changes must carry a `## Proof` section from the project's verification skill (`V-PROOF-01`); "unavailable" must name a concrete, checkable cause.
- New reviewer checks: subtract-before-add (`V-PAT-05`), destructive-operation idempotency (`V-SEC-14`), static UX checks (`V-UX-04` subset, `V-UX-05`, `V-UX-07`, `V-UX-08`), blast radius backed by an executed safety fact (`V-INT-05`), and an authz test for any new endpoint.

#### Safer hooks

- The bash write-target guard now catches writes outside the worktree through `>&path`, `&>path`, `>|`, `mv` sources, `cp`/`mv`/`ln -t` and `--target-directory`, `install` (including `-d`), `ln`, `truncate`, `dd of=` and `rsync` destinations. Unresolvable targets warn instead of passing silently.
- Quoted git subcommands, options and global flags (`git 'reset' --hard`, `git '-C' <dir> worktree remove …`) are now recognised by the main-clone and worktree-removal guards.
- The hook docs state why the local dev wrapper stays fail-open and that the shipped plugin hooks fail closed.

#### Pacing and resources

- The orchestrator reads Claude Code's statusline `rate_limits` to throttle, hold, scale up or pause spawning, with daily and five-hour budget compartments, a `pace-log.jsonl` record and a clean resume after a pause.
- A host-resource gate checks memory, load and I/O before test- or build-heavy batches.

#### Smaller fixes

- V-CITE-02 matches slash-shorthand V-codes (`V-SEC-01/02`) as whole tokens; V-TREE-01 also checks the build-tree audit coverage table; a shared state-file install helper; trimmed reviewer prompt; `--cwd`-pinned script invocations resolve to the plugin root.
